items.headline: Caveolin 1 is a conserved host factor mediating Bacillus cereus hemolysin BL toxin cytolytic toxicity
items.preview: Caveolin-1 has been identified as a crucial host factor for HBL toxin activity.
items.article:
Hemolysin BL (HBL) is a major virulence factor of Bacillus cereus, and while LITAF and CDIP1 have been recognized as host receptors for HBL, their absence only partially protects against the toxin. Recent research has identified caveolin-1 (CAV1) as an additional host factor necessary for HBL's cytolytic activity. 

Using genome-wide CRISPR knockout screens, it was shown that CAV1 colocalizes with HBL and is essential for the toxin's effects. Mice lacking all three factors (Litaf, CDIP1, and CAV1) exhibited complete resistance to HBL, highlighting the importance of CAV1 in B. cereus virulence. Why this matters: This discovery establishes a tripartite host factor system essential for HBL toxin activity, providing new insights into the mechanisms of bacterial virulence.

items.headline: Shareholder pressures Capricor; Lilly dives deeper into vaccines
items.preview: Capricor faces shareholder demands for governance changes amid FDA decision deadline.
items.article:
Activist investor Kaos Capital is pushing for a governance reset at Capricor Therapeutics just before an FDA decision on its Duchenne muscular dystrophy cell therapy. They are calling for a meeting to nominate new board directors and to freeze non-essential spending. 

In other news, Eli Lilly has partnered with Amplitude Therapeutics to develop trans-amplifying RNA vaccines, which may offer easier manufacturing and stronger potency. This collaboration is part of Lilly's broader strategy to enhance its vaccine research portfolio.

items.headline: Consensus Roadmap Guides Clinical Trials for Rare Childhood CNS Tumors
items.preview: A new roadmap aims to improve clinical trials for rare childhood CNS tumors.
items.article:
A multi-stakeholder consensus published in the British Journal of Cancer proposes a strategic roadmap to enhance clinical trials for rare childhood central nervous system tumors. The authors emphasize the need for international collaboration and flexible trial designs to accommodate the unique challenges posed by these rare diseases. 

The roadmap advocates for shared eligibility criteria and harmonized outcome measures to facilitate recruitment across borders, aiming to produce meaningful results despite the small patient populations involved. This approach is crucial for advancing treatment options for children with these complex conditions.

items.headline: Zanidatamab Shows Promise in Early-Stage HER2-Positive Breast Cancer Trial
items.preview: Zanidatamab is being tested as a neoadjuvant therapy for HER2-positive breast cancer.
items.article:
The NeoZanHER phase 2 trial investigates zanidatamab, a biparatopic antibody, in patients with early-stage HER2-positive breast cancer. This study aims to evaluate the antibody's dual engagement of HER2 to enhance treatment efficacy before surgery. 

The trial's design allows for real-time observation of tumor response, which could inform post-surgical treatment decisions. While the single-arm nature of the trial limits its ability to establish superiority over standard therapies, it represents a significant step in exploring innovative treatment strategies for aggressive breast cancer.

items.headline: Lab-grown brain models gain a sense of place
items.preview: New lab-grown brain models mimic regional identities of the human cortex.
items.article:
Researchers at UC Irvine have developed a method to create lab-grown human brain organoids that exhibit defined regional identities, mimicking the front and back areas of the cerebral cortex. This advancement allows for better understanding of brain development and disorders. 

By guiding the organoids with specific chemical signals, the team demonstrated that these models could replicate the molecular characteristics of different cortical regions. This innovation opens new avenues for studying neurodevelopmental disorders like fragile X syndrome, providing insights into how such conditions may disrupt normal brain organization.
